best_for: Modelers, animators and indie game artists on a recent Windows PC, Apple silicon Mac or Linux box who want a full 3D suite without a license fee.

points.title: No license fee, ever
points.text: Blender is free and open source under the GPL. You can use it for commercial work, and there is no paid edition.

points.title: Intel Macs stop at 4.x
points.text: Blender's manual says version 5.0 and later only support Macs with Apple silicon. An Intel Mac needs a 4.x release, which this site does not list for macOS; only the current release is kept there.

points.title: Windows on Arm is covered
points.text: Windows builds come for both x64 and Arm64. The installer listed here puts Blender in for all users and needs administrator rights. The zip from blender.org needs no admin rights and lets several versions sit side by side.

points.title: Many versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 56 versions, which helps when an add-on or a studio pipeline is pinned to an older release. macOS and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Linux: the Flatpak is not verified
points.text: The Flatpak listed here comes from Flathub, which does not mark it as verified, and it is x64 only. The manual's own Linux routes are the official tarball, Snap, and distribution packages, which it warns may lag or lack Cycles GPU rendering.
